title: Per-token P99 attribution and failover telemetry foundation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a telemetry foundation that attributes per-token latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) to the right routing and failure domains so SRE and product teams can make precise load-shedding and failover decisions. This work will: 1) capture lightweight per-token timing markers across the serving path (ingest, routing, queueing, kernel execution, kv-cache hit/miss), 2) attach region/availability-zone, model-variant, and circuit-breaker state to traces, and 3) expose aggregated rollups and drill-down dashboards for investigating tail behavior during cross-region incidents or circuit activations.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument per-token markers with <= 3% p99 overhead in staging load tests
Telemetry attaches routing metadata: region, model_variant, dedicated vs hosted, circuit_breaker_state
Grafana dashboards with: global p50/p95/p99 rollups, per-region heatmap, time-aligned circuit activation overlay
Ability to query token-level aggregates by arbitrary tag (model, region, instance_type) for last 14 days
Sampling strategy implemented: base sample 1% deterministic + adaptive capture of requests where backend latency > 95th percentile
Runbook entry for investigating token-level spikes and rolling a region-level failover is published and reviewed
implementation_plan: Spike: add lightweight timestamp markers at ingress, router decision, queue dequeue, kernel start/end, kv-cache hit/miss — implement as numeric tags to avoid heavy traces
Add routing metadata enrichment in the request router so downstream telemetry gets region/model/circuit info
Prototype storage: use existing timeseries rollup pipeline with new rollup keys per-token-percentile; avoid high-cardinality by bucketing and sampling
Dashboards: build a top-level rollup (global) and a regional matrix; add circuit overlay panel that pulls circuit state events from the circuit-control topic
Sampling & retention: base 1% deterministic sample for long-term trends; adaptive high-fidelity capture for requests crossing latency thresholds (p95 detection) stored for 7 days
Canary rollout: stage -> canary region (us-west-2) -> two additional regions -> global, monitor overhead and accuracy
Documentation: Confluence design doc, runbook, API for querying per-token aggregates, and a short changelog for SRE on emergency toggles
decisions: Use lightweight numeric markers instead of full spans to control cardinality and cost
Combine deterministic base sampling with adaptive captures for tail fidelity; do not attempt full-sampling in production due to cost
Attach circuit-breaker state at enrichment time rather than reprocessing traces to allow immediate correlation
Rollups will be limited to tag sets (region, model_variant, deployment_tier) — instance-level live debugging requires explicit trace capture
Store adaptive high-fidelity captures for 7 days; aggregated rollups for 90 days
updates: 2026-02-25: Spike complete — added markers in a branch; local microbench shows ~0.8% median latency overhead, p99 overhead around 2.6% under synthetic load
2026-03-02: Design review with Observability and Runtime teams — accepted numeric-marker approach, flagged concern around router enrichment path; runtime to send enrichment payload asynchronously
2026-03-05: Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7123 — implements markers + enrichment hooks; added unit tests for marker emission
2026-03-08: Load test in staging (10k rps synthetic): storage rollup pipeline accepted traffic; disk utilization increase +3% and Ingest API CPU +4% — still within budget
2026-03-10: Decided adaptive sampling thresholds: detect backend latency > p95 on 1-minute window, trigger full capture for that request and related requests from same routing bucket
2026-03-12: Dashboard draft created in Grafana: grafana.redwood.local/d/TTfSx2/per-token-telemetry-draft — shared with SRE and PM for feedback; next: add circuit overlay and link to runbook
